paper_title: Unifying Monopole and Center Vortex as the Semiclassical Confinement Mechanism (Hayashi, 2024, Physical Review Letters)
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.}
In the shift-twisted small-$L_3$ reduction of the monopole gas on $\mathbb{R}^2\times S^1$, the sum over the $N$ constant dual-photon vacua is
\[
Z_{3D}\simeq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp\left(2NVL_3\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right).
\]
Matching this branch weight to the two-dimensional center-vortex gas gives
\[
\zeta_v=NL_3\zeta_m.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & N\in\mathbb{Z},\ N\ge2,\quad V>0,\quad L_3>0,\quad \zeta_m>0,
\quad \theta\in\mathbb{R}.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle L_3\gg L_4\text{ and }L_3\text{ is small enough that the shifted compactification may be reduced}\\
& \displaystyle \text{to the }N\text{ constant saddles }\vec\sigma_k^*.\\[1mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle \{\vec e_1,\ldots,\vec e_N\}\text{ is an orthonormal basis,}\quad \vec E:=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\vec e_r.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle \vec\alpha_r:=\vec e_r-\vec e_{r+1}\quad(r=1,\ldots,N-1),\qquad
\vec\alpha_N:=-\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\vec\alpha_r.\\[3mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \vec\mu_j:=\sum_{s=1}^{j}\vec e_s-\frac{j}{N}\vec E\quad(j=1,\ldots,N-1),
\qquad \vec\rho:=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\vec\mu_j.\\[3mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle \vec\sigma_k^*:=\frac{2\pi k}{N}\vec\rho,
\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}_N:=\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}.\\[3mm]
\text{(P7)} & \displaystyle \mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma)=-\sum_{n=1}^{N}2\zeta_m
\cos\left(\vec\alpha_n\cdot\vec\sigma+\frac{\theta}{N}\right)\quad\text{for constant }\vec\sigma.\\[4mm]
\text{(P8)} & \displaystyle Z_{3D}\simeq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp\left(-\int d^3x\,\mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma_k^*)\right),
\qquad \int d^3x=VL_3.\\[4mm]
\text{(P9)} & \displaystyle \cos(a+2\pi r)=\cos a\quad\text{for all }a\in\mathbb{R},\ r\in\mathbb{Z}.\\[2mm]
\text{(P10)} & \displaystyle \text{The center-vortex branch weight has the form }
\exp\left(2V\zeta_v\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right).
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For $r,j\in\{1,\ldots,N-1\}$,
\begin{align}
\vec\alpha_r\cdot\vec\mu_j
&=(\vec e_r-\vec e_{r+1})\cdot\left(\sum_{s=1}^{j}\vec e_s-\frac{j}{N}\vec E\right)
&&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=(\vec e_r-\vec e_{r+1})\cdot\sum_{s=1}^{j}\vec e_s
-\frac{j}{N}(\vec e_r-\vec e_{r+1})\cdot\vec E
&&\text{linearity}\\
&=\left(\sum_{s=1}^{j}\delta_{rs}\right)-\left(\sum_{s=1}^{j}\delta_{r+1,s}\right)
&&\text{orthonormality and }(\vec e_r-\vec e_{r+1})\cdot\vec E=0\\
&=\begin{cases}1, & j=r,\\0, & j\ne r.
\end{cases}
\end{align}
Thus, for $r=1,\ldots,N-1$,
\begin{align}
\vec\alpha_r\cdot\vec\rho
&=\vec\alpha_r\cdot\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\vec\mu_j
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}\vec\alpha_r\cdot\vec\mu_j
&&\text{linearity}\\
&=1.
\end{align}
For the affine root,
\begin{align}
\vec\alpha_N\cdot\vec\rho
&=\left(-\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\vec\alpha_r\right)\cdot\vec\rho
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=-\sum_{r=1}^{N-1}\vec\alpha_r\cdot\vec\rho\\
&=-(N-1)\\
&=1-N.
\end{align}
Therefore, for every $n=1,\ldots,N$, there exists $q_n\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\begin{align}
\vec\alpha_n\cdot\vec\rho&=1+Nq_n.
\end{align}
At the saddle $\vec\sigma_k^*$,
\begin{align}
\vec\alpha_n\cdot\vec\sigma_k^*
&=\vec\alpha_n\cdot\left(\frac{2\pi k}{N}\vec\rho\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}(1+Nq_n)\\
&=\frac{2\pi k}{N}+2\pi kq_n.
\end{align}
Hence each monopole vertex has the same phase at a fixed saddle:
\begin{align}
\cos\left(\vec\alpha_n\cdot\vec\sigma_k^*+\frac{\theta}{N}\right)
&=\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}+2\pi kq_n\right)\\
&=\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}
&&\text{by (P9)}.
\end{align}
Substitution into the constant Lagrangian gives
\begin{align}
\mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma_k^*)
&=-\sum_{n=1}^{N}2\zeta_m\cos\left(\vec\alpha_n\cdot\vec\sigma_k^*+\frac{\theta}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=-\sum_{n=1}^{N}2\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\\
&=-2N\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}.
\end{align}
The action of the $k$th constant saddle is
\begin{align}
\int d^3x\,\mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma_k^*)
&=VL_3\mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma_k^*)
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=-2NVL_3\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
Z_{3D}
&\simeq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp\left(-\int d^3x\,\mathcal{L}_{3D}(\vec\sigma_k^*)\right)
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp\left(2NVL_3\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right).
\end{align}
Matching this branch weight with the center-vortex branch weight in (P10) yields
\begin{align}
2V\zeta_v&=2NVL_3\zeta_m,\\
\zeta_v&=NL_3\zeta_m
&&\text{since }V>0.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{Z_{3D}\simeq\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp\left(2NVL_3\zeta_m\cos\frac{\theta+2\pi k}{N}\right),\qquad \zeta_v=NL_3\zeta_m}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.}
For a fundamental Wilson loop $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, a vortex carrying flux $2\pi\vec\nu_n$ inside $C$ multiplies the loop by the center element $e^{-2\pi i/N}$, whereas no enclosed flux gives phase $1$:
\[
W(C)=
\begin{cases}
e^{-2\pi i/N}, & \text{vortex lies inside }C,\\
1, & \text{vortex lies outside }C.
\end{cases}
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & N\in\mathbb{Z},\ N\ge2.\\[1mm]
\text{(P2)} & \displaystyle \{\vec e_1,\ldots,\vec e_N\}\text{ is an orthonormal basis of }\mathbb{R}^N,
\quad \vec E:=\sum_{r=1}^{N}\vec e_r.\\[2mm]
\text{(P3)} & \displaystyle \vec\nu_m:=\vec e_m-\frac{1}{N}\vec E,
\qquad m=1,\ldots,N.\\[2mm]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle W(C):=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{m=1}^{N}\exp\left(i\vec\nu_m\cdot\int_C\vec a\right).\\[3mm]
\text{(P5)} & \displaystyle \int_C\vec a=
\begin{cases}
2\pi\vec\nu_n, & \text{vortex lies inside }C,\\
0, & \text{vortex lies outside }C.
\end{cases}\\[5mm]
\text{(P6)} & \displaystyle e^{2\pi i}=1.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First compute the inner products of the defining weights:
\begin{align}
\vec\nu_m\cdot\vec\nu_n
&=\left(\vec e_m-\frac{1}{N}\vec E\right)\cdot\left(\vec e_n-\frac{1}{N}\vec E\right)
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\vec e_m\cdot\vec e_n-\frac{1}{N}\vec e_m\cdot\vec E-\frac{1}{N}\vec E\cdot\vec e_n+\frac{1}{N^2}\vec E\cdot\vec E\\
&=\delta_{mn}-\frac{1}{N}-\frac{1}{N}+\frac{N}{N^2}
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\delta_{mn}-\frac{1}{N}.
\end{align}
Case 1: the vortex lies inside $C$.  Then
\begin{align}
W(C)
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{m=1}^{N}\exp\left(i\vec\nu_m\cdot2\pi\vec\nu_n\right)
&&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{m=1}^{N}\exp\left(2\pi i\left(\delta_{mn}-\frac{1}{N}\right)\right)
&&\text{by the inner-product formula}\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\left[\exp\left(2\pi i\left(1-\frac{1}{N}\right)\right)+\sum_{\substack{m=1\\m\ne n}}^{N}\exp\left(-\frac{2\pi i}{N}\right)\right]
&&\text{separate }m=n\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\left[e^{2\pi i}e^{-2\pi i/N}+(N-1)e^{-2\pi i/N}\right]\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\left[e^{-2\pi i/N}+(N-1)e^{-2\pi i/N}\right]
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=e^{-2\pi i/N}.
\end{align}
Case 2: the vortex lies outside $C$.  Then
\begin{align}
W(C)
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{m=1}^{N}\exp\left(i\vec\nu_m\cdot0\right)
&&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{m=1}^{N}1\\
&=1.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{W(C)=
\begin{cases}
e^{-2\pi i/N}, & \text{vortex lies inside }C,\\
1, & \text{vortex lies outside }C.
\end{cases}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
